citations.review_text: empire at war is a gem, the space combat of it is incredible, for a game as old as it is the gameplay holds up fairly well, multiplayer is super fun, ground combat is a little bit of a coin toss in quality, but watching your swarm of Y-wings and B-wings fire everything they have at a star destroyers shield generator is always satisfying, one of my favorite parts is for ship to ship combat, you get to decide what you want to hit, if you want to take out their weapons, go for it, their engines, why not. and thats part of what makes this game great. and the modding scene for this game keeps it alive, theres so many great mods for any star wars fan of any era. Worth the money but goes on sale super often for cheap too

This game until a few years ago would barely function; now after some great patch work, it runs great, has mod support, and plays like what I dreamed it would when I got the original Empire at War and Forces of Corruption back at Best Buy 2 decades ago.

While this is far from the best Grand Strategy Game, it is incredibly enjoyable. The land combat feels dated but fun but the space combat still feels very modern and incredibly fun. The story is rather good, and the grand campaign is robust.

It would be a dream to get a sequel to this and Galactic Battleground with all of the prequel / sequel / original trilogy / other games, but if this is all we get, it is fantastic enough. Now... get ready to fire the Death Star!

If you've ever wanted to command a Star Destroyer fleet or stage a massive planetary invasion, this is your dream game. The space battles are magnificent, cinematic spectacles where targeting specific ship subsystems actually matters, even if the ground combat feels a bit clunky by comparison. Thanks to a legendary modding community that keeps it alive with massive total conversions, the replay value here is practically infinite.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that community-made mods available on the Steam Workshop are essential for extending the game's content and playability.

citations.review_text: This game has aged beautifully, whilst teh base game is fun in iteself, where it really shiens is in the modpacks, You can do naything from survival gamemodes to full campaigns or just pit two customised fleets agaisnt eachother. I highly recomend.

If you love the original Star Wars Battlefront games, this is essentially the RTS version, featuring very fun space and land battles with many maps. Objectively, the smooth controls, high fidelity zoom and camera adjustment make this one of the best in the RTS genre for pc. On top of this, the modding community takes a rather content limited game after a couple dozen hours, and gives you hundreds of hours of content to enjoy. Every era of star wars from the old republic to the new republic can be controlled in space and in land, with thousands of troop options and hundreds game modes. This is one of those games I wish I had played for all of my life. 10/10 make sure to try the community mods that make this game so lovable even after 20 years since release.

The base game shows its age. The AI is dumb, the pathfinding is janky, and the campaign balance leaves a lot to be desired by modern RTS standards. If you're coming in expecting something that plays as smoothly as current strategy titles, you'll probably be disappointed.

That said, the modding community is where this game truly shines. Years after release, people are still building and updating massive overhauls that add new factions, rebalance the economy, expand the galaxy map, and bring in eras and content that never made it into the vanilla game. Some of these mods are more polished and content rich than a lot of full price releases.

I'm a big fan of the Clone Wars era, and this is genuinely one of the best places to experience it in game form. There are several excellent mods dedicated to that period, with detailed unit rosters, iconic ships, and campaigns that capture the feel of the era in a way few other games manage.

If you're buying this purely for the base game, temper your expectations. If you're buying it as a foundation for mods, this is an easy recommend. Just know upfront that you'll want to spend time in the Workshop and mod forums to get the most out of it.

Recommended, with the mod community doing most of the heavy lifting.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that space battles are enjoyable while land battles are less well received.

citations.review_text: Space Battles are great land battle are not.

"Empire at War" is a true "Star Wars" gem, but you have to stick with it for a while before it starts to shine. At first I was discouraged by how hectic the galactic map management and the battles were while I was still trying to make heads or tails of things. Even now I'm not quite sure why the game ended up working so well for me. The story is average at best, the maps are all very small and quite repetitive, and I kept using "auto-resolve" more often than I would have liked. Then came the gradual switch from the pause button to the fast-forward button to speed things along. But despite all its flaws, I found the space battles extremely addictive. The eternal 12-year-old within me got giddy whenever Mon Calamari Cruisers clashed with Imperial Star Destroyers, targeting the capital ships' hardpoints all while the iconic John Williams soundtrack kept blasting in the background. The mayhem, the joy!

claims.claim: The game features active multiplayer functionality on the Steam version.

citations.review_text: This game has always been my favorite strategy game since childhood. Its probably the only good Star Wars strategy game and its basically 2 games in 1. Not only that, the mods this game has can be considered their very own game aswell like Thrawn's Revenge, Republic at war, etc. The storyline seems to be enjoyable with each faction having their own mechanics and unique units to control. Soundtrack is pretty good, especially the ones in Force of Corruption. Multiplayer for this steam version is still around, so can play with friends or other players if you so choose or stick with Skirmish with the bots.

English Version (french below)

Now that game was my childhood. Lots of units / warships, 3 campaigns including the Forces of Corruption, each with very different factions, and an awful lot of available mods that really enhances the game.
Of course the music is very nice, the graphics are... okay (but they are way better for space battles)
You can also play online with other players, which is very fun.

Only real problem I have with this game is that game balancing was thrown out of the window. The empire has the same tool as the rebels, but has also better options, better ships, better heroes and better vehicles. And let's not get started on the Death Star or Darth Vader's ship in Forces of Corruption because that's a whole other level.
And I'll admit that after playing games like Warcraft 3 or Battle for Middle Earth, the lack of levelling or unlockable abilities for heroes kind of hurts the game a little.

Apart from that, yeah the game is a lot of fun !



Version Française : 

Alors là, ce jeu c'est mon enfance. Plein d'unités, de véhicules et de vaisseaux, 3 campagnes différentes en incluant Forces of Corruption, chacune avec des factions uniques et plein de mods disponibles qui améliorent nettement le jeu.

Le seul problème que j'ai, c'est que l'équilibrage a vraiment été balancé par la fenêtre. L'empire a des meilleurs unités, des meilleures véhicules, des meilleurs vaisseaux et des meilleurs héros, et on va pas lancer le sujet de l'Etoile Noire ou du croiseur de Vador dans Forces of Corruption.
Aussi, j'avoue qu'après avoir joué à Warcraft 3 et La Bataille pour la Terre du Milieu, ca fait mal de ne pas avoir de niveaux et de compétences débloquables / améliorables sur les héros.

A part ça, le jeu est très cool !

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game can experience crashes when running mods.

citations.review_text:
This game is my childhood.
Back when I was a kid, I remember waking up early on Saturdays to watch my Dad play this game. That was my form of entertainment.
When I got older and was able to play it myself, I remember spending an hour every day just either dominating the campaign with Urai Fen or Garm Bel Iblis, or playing on the Kamino Skirmish map, afking after setting up a impenetrable defense at my base just to see how many enemy units gets destroyed in that limited time frame. (I was a kid, my parents only allowed 1 hour of computer time a day.)

But fast forward just a couple years ago, I discovered modding and tried out a few mods for the game. They were really fun and exciting to see and play new things. But overtime it became a bit overwhelming and I missed the base game.

Then, I discovered the XML files. Not only I removed Han Solo's voice line where he sweared every single time he died... which happened very often. But I got to read and discover hidden dev messages left during development which was fun.

What started out as just increasing the health of the Defilers, childishly pretending it was my OC, I eventually learned how to give them new abilities, how to change their name, and I kept on experimenting. I discovered what not to do to prevent the game from crashing when booting up, I learned how smart it is to have backups of the original files, and I kept on making changes.

When I returned to mods, I began to copy the textures/models/files from various characters or units that I liked and started putting them into my reworked version. Eventually... I started just developing my own mod just for fun. While I probably won't publish it, due to being unable to track down the original artists for the models I was using, I will still continue to mod the game while keeping the original foundation of the vanilla version.

Honestly, 1.1k hours on this game makes sense. I never get tired of it, I love playing it, and it has been a huge part of my entertainment…
Love the game but mods crash alot.
